title: Plan fallback crediting and per-route degradation PRD
creator: Jasmine Patel
description: Enable safe, auditable plan fallback behavior when a customer exceeds per-route or per-plan limits and implement an automated crediting adjudication flow that can 1) apply pro-rated credits for partially served requests, 2) generate invoice adjustments, and 3) produce clear end-user communications. This PRD covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, telemetry, rollout, and billing acceptance tests.
background: Customers on usage-based plans and hybrid reserved plans have reported confusing invoices and support tickets when we throttle or silently degrade routes during quota contention. Existing burst and soft-cap mechanisms reduce outages but do not produce deterministic invoice adjustments or customer-facing explanations when requests are intentionally routed to lower-cost or lower-capacity model variants. Support costs are increasing and finance needs a reproducible adjudication policy for refunds and credits.
goals: 1) Define deterministic fallback rules across per-route, per-model, and per-tenant quotas. 2) Automatically calculate and apply credits for requests that were partially processed due to degradation (e.g., truncated responses, shortened context). 3) Surface clear billing metadata on invoices and in the Console. 4) Provide audit logs and an appeals path for customers.
success_metrics: - Reduction in billing-related support tickets by 40% in 90 days after rollout. - Invoice adjustments automated for 90% of fallback-related cases. - SLO: credit calculation latency < 2s for real-time adjudication; nightly batch reconciliation completes in < 2 hours. - Telemetry: 99% of fallback events contain the required billing metadata fields.
non_goals: This PRD does not change overall pricing tiers or introduce new public SKUs. It also excludes long-term manual refund workflows; those remain in finance scope. It does not modify model-level token accounting (tokenization rules remain).
proposed_design: - Policy engine updates: add a 'fallback_class' taxonomy (grace, degraded, redirected) with deterministic mapping rules. - Billing metadata: attach billing_tags to each request when fallback is applied (tag format: fallback_class=<name>; original_sku=<sku>; effective_sku=<sku>; served_tokens=<n>; requested_tokens=<n>). - Credit rules: define formulas per fallback_class (e.g., degraded: credit = (1 - served_tokens/requested_tokens) * request_price). - Transaction flow: real-time credits for CLI/Console operations via a 'provisional credit' ledger entry; nightly reconciliation job converts provisional credits into invoice adjustments. - Audit trail: immutable events in event-store with links to Console view and downloadable CSV. - UI: Console shows per-invoice line with 'fallback' flag, credit amount, and reference ID with link to decision log.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): routing + metadata only; no automated credits (2 weeks). Phase 2 (pilot): apply provisional credits for a small set of enterprise customers and surface invoice line items (4 weeks). Phase 3 (ramp): expand to all Hosted API users with opt-out for legacy customers (3 weeks). Phase 4: full default behavior and nightly reconciliation + finance integration (2 weeks). Each phase gated by acceptance tests and finance sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine emits fallback_class and billing_tags for 100% of routed requests when fallback occurs.
Console exposes a fallback incidents view filtered by customer, date range, and fallback_class.
Provisional credit ledger entries are created for each qualifying degraded request with correct computed amount per formula.
Nightly reconciliation job converts provisional credits to invoice adjustments with no more than 5% mismatch rate versus expected amounts.
All fallback events are queryable in audit logs and include request_id, user_id, original_sku, effective_sku, requested_tokens, served_tokens, credit_amount, and decision_rule_id.
Support playbook documented and shared with SRE/CS/Finance teams and validated in a runbook tabletop exercise.
billing_acceptance_criteria: For a sample of 1000 degraded requests, computed credits match manual audit within tolerance of ±1%.
Invoices generated post-reconciliation include a human-readable description of credit reasons and the reference ID linking to the audit event.
Edge-case tests: partial-batch processing and truncated streaming responses produce correct credit amounts and do not double-credit.
Finance systems receive invoice adjustments via the existing billing integration within the agreed SLA (24 hours for batch import).
Chargeback metrics in internal dashboards reflect credits and do not negatively affect reserved capacity accounting (reserved commitments remain unchanged).
telemetry_and_alerting: - Counters: fallback_events_total by fallback_class, customer, route; provisional_credits_total and sum(credit_amount). - Gauges: provisional_ledger_size, reconciliation_backlog_seconds. - Alerts: reconciliation_backlog > 6 hours (P0), mismatch_rate > 5% over 1 day (P1), missing_billing_tags_rate > 0.5% (P1). - Dashboards: per-customer fallback timeline with correlated latency and error metrics.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-crediting could lead to financial loss. Mitigation: start with pilot limited customers, include manual approval threshold for credits > $500/day per customer, and implement reconciliation checks. Risk: customer confusion about visible credits. Mitigation: include templated communication and Console explainer with examples.
open_questions: What is the canonical definition of 'served_tokens' for streaming responses that were truncated by fallback?
Should we allow merchants to opt into a credit-only mode (visible credits but no invoice adjustments) for a soft rollout?
What threshold should trigger manual finance review for delta > $X/day? Proposal: $500/day.
